facts.fact: The Department of Communications and Digital Technologies published the National Policy on Data and Cloud as Notice 2533 of 2024 in Government Gazette 50741 on 31 May 2024; it covers national and provincial government and organs of state, and sets out government's position on cloud-based long-term data storage and compute.
facts.system: National Policy on Data and Cloud

facts.fact: The policy says government data shall be stored in unified, cloud-enabled data centres with redundancies in designated locations, names the State Information Technology Agency (SITA) as the authority to source data infrastructure and cloud services for government, and says departments and entities shall prioritise cloud as the primary option for new ICT procurement; no list of providers or of specific hosting is given in this text (date is the document's published date).
facts.system: National Policy on Data and Cloud

systems.owner: SITA (sources infrastructure and cloud services for government)

facts.fact: President Ramaphosa said in March 2025 that government published the National Data and Cloud Policy the previous year (2024); the document gives no month.

slug: 2024-10-11 South Africa's Significant Improvement in the UN e-Government Index 2024

facts.fact: The DCDT statement lists 'the drafting of the Data and Cloud Strategy' among contributors to South Africa's UN e-government ranking; it gives no event date, so the document's published date of 2024-10-11 is used.

ENSafrica reports the DCDT officially published the National Data and Cloud Policy (Government Gazette No. 50741) on 31 May 2024 under section 3(1) of the Electronic Communications Act, 2005, applying to national and provincial government, organs of state and the private sector.

ENSafrica says the policy aims to migrate all government IT services to the cloud via decentralised private providers, requires government data centre infrastructure to be in the country, names no government cloud or provider list, and still needs implementation through consultation with SITA and departments (as of 10 June 2024).
